whatItIs.text: Corn tortillas cut into triangles and fried or baked — nixtamalized corn, which is what separates them from plain corn chips.

historyNote.text: The triangle chip was popularised in the 1940s by Rebecca Webb Carranza, who cut the misshapen tortillas rejected by her Los Angeles factory's machine into triangles and sold them a dime a bag; nachos themselves were invented in 1943 by Ignacio Anaya in Piedras Negras, Mexico.

howToChoose.text: Choose thick, whole-grain, or restaurant-style chips for dipping strength; check the fry oil — frying in good oil (and draining) keeps flavour clean.

storage.text: Reseal tightly at room temperature; they lose crunch before anything else.

useItUp.text: Turn the last chips into chilaquiles, nachos, or a crunchy salad topper.
